evidence_scope: The package documents a supplied training guide. The guide contains written instructions, checkpoints, callouts, a testing checklist and a troubleshooting table, but no screenshots, figures or recorded test results. Content is described as what the guide describes, the expected behavior and the intended outcome. Personal execution of the lab and successful outcomes are not verified.
not_included: Screenshots or rendered PDF pages presented as screenshots
Ticket IDs, account names, timestamps or event log exports
Test results, resolved tickets or completed account changes
Approval records, caller-verification procedures or escalation outcomes
Passwords, enrollment QR codes, MFA seeds, recovery codes or other credentials
screenshots_note: Intentionally empty. The source PDF contains no embedded images (0 on each of its 14 pages) and no numbered figures. No screenshots were created, substituted or rendered from PDF pages.

page_references.content: Title, attribution, why the lab matters, learning objectives
Prerequisites (Labs 1-4, Authentik admin access), HTTP note, menu-label callout
Section 01: triage, Events > Logs, deliberate failed logins, Checkpoint 1
Ticket zero: verify the caller (no procedure defined by the guide)
Section 02: Ticket 1, password reset, recovery-link callout, Checkpoint 2
Section 03: Ticket 2, lockout versus deactivation, log callout, escalation, lab-only reactivation, Checkpoint 3
Section 04: Ticket 3, authenticator removal and re-enrollment, exemption callout, Checkpoint 4
Section 05: Ticket 4, authentication versus authorization, mover path, shortcut callouts, tile cache

limitations.detail: The goal and testing checklist describe a credential the analyst never learns, but the lab has no recovery flow and falls back to an admin-set password. The documentation does not claim an analyst-unknown password.

The finding that a correct password against an inactive account produces login_failed, indistinguishable from a wrong password, is the guide's report for its environment and is not independently verified.
The guide reactivates the leaver for later labs. It is documented as a controlled training step separate from the production response (escalation) and is not claimed as performed.
The guide requires following the organization's standard but does not define one.
The guide requires an expiry and a note for any temporary exemption; no approval flow is defined.
The 24-hour tile-cache behavior and workaround are stated for the source environment only.
The troubleshooting row on wrong WordPress permissions depends on group-based role mapping from Lab 4. Plugin tier support and the role configuration need confirmation.
No Authentik, OrangeHRM or WordPress version is stated; menu labels may differ.
